history.gap: The spec table is tidy but generic: tracked small-cap labels, dashed rules and a gold italic are a competent editorial kit, not a signature. The hairlines are not even consistent — the dashed rule under the Discord row runs ~40px further right than the three above it, and only the tagline rule carries the gold tint, so the grid reads as accidental. At the bar, every rule would end on the same column, the label column would be tied to a real grid module, and one element (the tagline, the mono link, the 01 marker) would be pushed hard enough to be the thing you remember.
history.motion: Staggered row fades and a blur-to-sharp reveal with a slow gold progress hairline — restrained and readable, though frame 1 shows the chart panel slicing through the headline mid-transition.
history.verdict: A is a quiet, well-typeset spec table with a few hairline inconsistencies and no real signature; B is far more ambitious but arrives with clipped labels, nav artifacts, a mobile dead zone and broken word spacing, none of which survive a Site of the Day jury. A wins on execution; neither is shortlist-ready as-is.

history.gap: The production block is a well-set but modest four-row spec list, and its one system (dotted gold leaders running from the frame rule into right-aligned small-cap labels) is thrown away on mobile for a generic centred stack; keep the label/leader logic at 390px (label left in small caps, value on the next line with the leader still terminating at a rule) so the section reads as the same object. Also fix the rhythm details: the "Discord" row with its underlined mono URL is taller than the other three and the "01 PRODUCTIE" rules start inboard of the vertical frame lines and are not symmetric about the label; at the bar the hairlines meet the frame and every row sits on the same baseline grid.
history.motion: Restrained blur-in fades, staggered row reveals and a nav label that morphs to "OPEN DE DISCORD" on scroll; competent, though the hero heading collides with the chart panel mid-scroll.
history.verdict: A wins on discipline: tight small-cap tracking, a considered leader system, a gold accent used once, and no visible bugs, even if the section is essentially a handsome data table rather than a designed moment. B reaches for a mood A never attempts, but unreadable copy, colliding rail labels, a struck-through mobile nav and a dead zone are disqualifying at Site of the Day level.
